context: The prompt requests a standalone web-based editor for the technical design schema JSON file. This editor needs to handle file system operations, provide CRUD capabilities for schema questions, and maintain visual consistency with the existing Technical Design page. Several implementation details need clarification to ensure the editor meets user expectations.

questions.question-text: How should the editor handle file system access for reading and writing the schema JSON file?

options.label: Simple HTTP server with REST API endpoints for file operations
options.pros: Clean separation of concerns, standard HTTP patterns, easy to test, allows file operations across different file system types
options.cons: Requires running a server process, more complex architecture, needs server startup/shutdown handling

options.label: Use browser's File System Access API with manual file selection
options.pros: No server required, runs entirely in browser, simpler architecture, better security through user-controlled file access
options.cons: User must manually select file on each load, no automatic file path persistence, limited browser support for older browsers

options.label: Python-based local server with file watching and auto-reload
options.pros: Automatic file change detection, can leverage existing Python codebase patterns, robust file handling
options.cons: Creates dependency on Python despite prompt's independence requirement, more complex to set up and maintain

questions.recommendation-rationale: A simple HTTP server provides the best balance between functionality and simplicity. It allows reliable file operations while keeping the frontend code clean. This approach is consistent with the existing Web UI server pattern in the framework and doesn't violate the independence requirement since it would be a standalone server specific to this editor.

questions.question-text: What layout structure should the editor use for organizing and displaying schema content?

options.label: Two-panel layout: tree navigation on left, question editor on right
options.pros: Clear visual hierarchy, familiar pattern for users, easy navigation between categories and questions, space-efficient
options.cons: Less screen space for editing, may require scrolling for long question forms

options.label: Single-page layout with collapsible sections for categories and questions
options.pros: All content visible in one view, simple scrolling navigation, good for overview and searching
options.cons: Can become cluttered with many questions, harder to focus on editing a single question, more scrolling required

options.label: Tab-based layout with separate tabs for categories
options.pros: Clean separation of categories, full width for editing, reduces visual clutter
options.cons: Harder to navigate between categories, no overview of all categories at once, more clicks to switch contexts

questions.recommendation-rationale: The two-panel layout with tree navigation is recommended because it provides the best user experience for editing a hierarchical schema. It matches the pattern described in P-001's implementation where categories are listed in a left sidebar, making it familiar to users of the Technical Design page. This layout allows quick navigation while keeping the editor interface focused.

questions.question-text: How should the editor handle CSS styling from the Technical Design page?

options.label: Copy the CSS file directly into the editor folder
options.pros: Complete independence, no external dependencies, editor works standalone, changes to original CSS don't break editor
options.cons: Duplicate code, manual sync needed for style updates, potential divergence over time

options.label: Reference the existing CSS file using relative path
options.pros: No duplication, automatic updates when main CSS changes, maintains single source of truth
options.cons: Creates a dependency on the Web UI structure, violates independence requirement, editor breaks if CSS file moves

options.label: Extract and adapt only the relevant CSS rules needed for the editor
options.pros: Minimal code, focused styling, independence maintained, can customize for editor-specific needs
options.cons: Requires manual extraction work, may miss some styling rules, need to identify which rules are relevant

questions.recommendation-rationale: Copying the CSS file directly is recommended because the prompt explicitly states the editor should be 'entirely independent from the scripts in .rdd and .rdd-instance folders'. This independence requirement suggests a standalone tool that should work even if moved to a different location or used in isolation. Copying the CSS ensures complete independence while maintaining the same look and feel.

questions.question-text: What level of schema validation should the editor provide when saving changes?

options.label: Basic JSON syntax validation only
options.pros: Simple to implement, fast validation, prevents corrupted JSON files, allows flexibility in schema structure
options.cons: Doesn't catch schema structure errors, may allow invalid question formats, could create runtime issues later

options.label: Full schema structure validation against expected format
options.pros: Prevents invalid schemas, catches errors early, ensures schema is usable by Technical Design page, better data integrity
options.cons: More complex implementation, need to define validation rules, might reject valid but unusual structures

options.label: No validation - save directly with user confirmation
options.pros: Maximum flexibility, fastest implementation, allows any structure changes, no validation code needed
options.cons: High risk of creating invalid schemas, no safety net for user errors, debugging issues becomes harder

questions.recommendation-rationale: Full schema structure validation is recommended to ensure the editor produces valid schemas that can be consumed by the Technical Design page implementation. Since the schema has a defined structure with categories, groups, questions, and conditional visibility rules, validating against this structure prevents errors that would only be discovered later during runtime. This improves the overall developer experience and reduces debugging time.

questions.question-text: Should the editor support editing conditional visibility rules (visibleWhen) for questions?

options.label: Full visual editor for conditional rules with dropdown builders
options.pros: User-friendly, prevents syntax errors, visual representation of logic, accessible to non-technical users
options.cons: Complex to implement, requires parsing and generating rule expressions, may limit advanced rule capabilities

options.label: Text-based editor with syntax highlighting and validation
options.pros: Flexible for complex rules, faster to implement, allows any rule expression, familiar to developers
options.cons: Requires knowledge of rule syntax, more error-prone for users, less discoverable for beginners

options.label: Simple enable/disable toggle - no conditional rules editing
options.pros: Very simple implementation, avoids complexity, reduces potential for errors, faster development
options.cons: Major limitation on editor functionality, conditional rules mentioned in P-001 as important feature, reduced utility

questions.recommendation-rationale: A text-based editor with syntax highlighting is recommended as it provides the necessary functionality for editing conditional rules while keeping the implementation manageable. Since this is a tool for developers editing the schema (not end-users filling out the technical design), a text-based approach is appropriate. This allows full flexibility in defining complex conditional logic while providing helpful visual feedback to prevent syntax errors.
